summary.one_liner: A Software Engineering Daily podcast episode page in which Atlassian's head of site reliability engineering, Mike Hiraga, discusses SRE, the evolution of operations work, and Atlassian's migration to the cloud.
use_cases: Learning how SRE evolved from sysadmin roles
Hearing how Atlassian approached moving to the cloud
Background reading on managing reliability at scale
Finding SRE culture material for a team
summary.what_it_does: The page is a podcast episode description and partial transcript summary. It traces how operations work moved from managing physical servers in the 1990s to virtualized, cloud-based, code-driven infrastructure. It explains that SRE focuses on making web applications more reliably available, especially for business software other companies depend on. The guest, Mike Hiraga, heads SRE at Atlassian, which makes JIRA, Confluence, HipChat and Bitbucket. The episode covers Atlassian's migration of its applications to the cloud.
notable: Interview with Atlassian's head of SRE about running reliability at massive scale
Covers Atlassian's move from pre-cloud infrastructure to the cloud
Historical overview of sysadmin to SRE and DevOps roles
Listed in the awesome-sre list under 'Culture'
caveats: Page text is a short episode description; the full transcript is not included
Atlassian is named as a sponsor of the show and is recruiting, as disclosed on the page
